overall_summary: Analysis of the recent historical data shows a clear shift in audience engagement. While older videos focused broadly on 'overthinking' and late-night feelings yielding low views (5-20 views), newer content centered around 'self respect'—specifically actions involving chat interactions, blocking, deleting, and status lists—consistently performs better (averaging 30-40 views, peaking at 40). The audience responds strongly to tactile, everyday digital boundary-setting rather than abstract sadness.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'चैट डिलीट करने की हिम्मत' (40 views), 'ब्लू टिक्स आज छिपा दिए' (34 views), and 'स्टेटस लिस्ट से उसका नाम' (33 views) consistently outperform abstract emotional content.
winning_patterns.action: Focus story hooks on micro-actions involving smartphone interfaces related to self-respect and moving on.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing heavily on generic time markers or abstract thoughts like 'रात के दो बजे' (12 views) or 'मेज पर रखी चाय ठंडी हो गई' (5 views) show very low traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely atmospheric openings without a specific, relatable modern conflict.

next_video.concept: A realization moment when clearing out phone galleries or archived folders where an old shared photo is finally deleted instead of saved to cloud storage.
next_video.opening_direction: Gallery clean-up notification: 'Deleting 500 items from Recently Deleted.'
next_video.twist_direction: Realizing the final photo isn't being deleted with tears, but with a blank, indifferent stare because the memory finally lost its weight.
next_video.reason: Aligns with the proven self-respect and digital cleanup winning pattern while slightly testing a gallery/media cleanup angle instead of just chats.

experiment: Testing whether shifting the self-respect tactile hook from chat apps (WhatsApp/Instagram) to phone storage/photo galleries retains the higher view counts.
